name: Shell / History-Window Unification Probe
purpose: Test whether shell cut (spatial: inside vs outside constraint surface) and history-window cut (temporal: current vs history) reduce to the same mathematical object I_c(A;B) = S(A) - S(AB). Bridge object Xi_hist: I_c(current; history) = I_c(inside-shell; outside-shell).
bridge_claim: shell/history unification via I_c bipartition equivalence

pytorch.reason: load-bearing: partial trace via reshape, VNE via eigvalsh, autograd for dI_c/dk in P3

pyg.reason: no graph message passing in this entropy sim

z3.reason: load-bearing: UNSAT proof that pure-state shell/hist sign contradiction is impossible (N1); UNSAT proof that product state I_c > 0 is impossible (N2)

cvc5.reason: z3 sufficient for these linear arithmetic UNSAT proofs

sympy.reason: supportive: formal I_c = S(A) - S(AB) expression confirms that shell and history cut labels produce identical algebraic objects

clifford.reason: no geometric algebra layer in this entropy sim

rustworkx.reason: no graph traversal or path computation required in this probe

xgi.reason: no hypergraph structure required; probe uses standard matrix operations

bell_state_shell_cut.note: Pure Bell state: I_c(shell cut) = I_c(history cut) = log(2)

werner_markov_chain_cut_equivalence.note: Werner state is symmetric under A<->B swap; shell cut and history cut agree exactly

bell_state_permutation.note: Pure state: S(AB)=0 and S(A)=S(B), so I_c(A;B)=I_c(B;A)

asymmetric_pure_2x3.note: Pure state 2x3: S(A)=S(B) still holds (Schmidt), so I_c(A;B)=I_c(B;A) regardless of dimension

ic_values_by_memory_depth.note: I_c increases monotonically with memory depth k: k=0 is product, k=3 is Bell

autograd_dIc_dk_at_k1p5.note: autograd confirms dI_c/dk > 0 at k=1.5; history depth increases coherent information

z3_pure_state_sign_contradiction.encoding: pure_state(S_AB=0) AND S_A=S_B(Schmidt) AND S_A>=0 AND S_B>=0 AND I_c_shell>0 AND I_c_hist<0
z3_pure_state_sign_contradiction.interpretation: UNSAT: For pure state, S_A=S_B and both are nonneg, so I_c_shell and I_c_hist cannot have opposite signs. Shell/history unification is structurally enforced.

z3_negative_control_mixed_state_sign_dif.encoding: mixed_state(S_AB>0) AND S_AB<=S_A+S_B AND S_A>=0 AND S_B>=0 AND I_c_shell=S_A-S_AB>0 AND I_c_hist=S_B-S_AB<0 (NO pure/symmetry constraint)
z3_negative_control_mixed_state_sign_dif.interpretation: SAT: For mixed state without Schmidt symmetry, I_c(shell) > 0 and I_c(hist) < 0 is achievable. N1 UNSAT relies on BOTH pure_state AND S_A=S_B (Schmidt) — removing either allows sign disagreement.

z3_product_state_ic_positive_unsat.encoding: product_state(S_AB=S_A+S_B) AND S_A>=0 AND S_B>=0 AND I_c=S_A-S_AB AND I_c>0
z3_product_state_ic_positive_unsat.interpretation: UNSAT: For product state, I_c = -S_B <= 0 always. This is cut-independent: whether labelled 'shell' or 'history', a product state cannot have positive I_c. Cut-independence IS the shell/history unification claim.

z3_entangled_state_negative_control.encoding: entangled(S_AB < S_A+S_B) AND S_A>=0 AND S_B>=0 AND I_c=S_A-S_AB AND S_A>S_AB AND I_c>0
z3_entangled_state_negative_control.interpretation: SAT: Entangled state can have I_c > 0. Product-state UNSAT is not trivially true for all states.

k0_memoryless_shell_ic.note: k=0 product state: I_c=0 for both cuts; shell and history cuts agree at boundary

kmax_full_memory_shell_ic.note: k=3 Bell state: I_c = log(2) = S(A) for both cuts; shell and history cuts agree at maximal memory

sympy_formal_expression.note: Sympy confirms: I_c(shell) and I_c(hist) are the same algebraic expression S_A - S_AB with different semantic labels. The structural equivalence is a tautology once cuts are defined as bipartitions.

caveat: Step 6 bridge. Shell/history cuts are candidate-equivalent; this is not promoted to canonical without Steps 1-5 evidence. Structural impossibility proofs (z3 UNSAT) are load-bearing; numeric tests are candidate witnesses.
